text:
Marathon Petroleum fell slightly today, snapping a three-day winning streak, as crude oil prices pulled back from their recent highs. Brent crude had spiked above $109 on Monday amid escalating Middle East tensions—Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and threats from Iran—but those geopolitical premiums appear to have cooled somewhat by end-of-week. The stock had surged 9% over the past two weeks riding that oil rally, so today's modest retreat is more of a pause than a reversal.

Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity and oil inventories remain relatively tight, which supports refinery margins when crude prices hold firm. The uncertainty now is whether the Middle East situation will flare up again or stabilize; if tensions ease and oil prices retreat further, refiners like MPC could face margin pressure, whereas another escalation could reignite the rally that drove the stock up so sharply.
